content.title: Antiplatelet therapy recommendations (excerpt)
recommendations: Aspirin recommended for all patients without contraindications: initial oral LD 150–300 mg (or 75–250 mg i.v.) and MD 75–100 mg o.d. for long-term treatment.
In all ACS patients, a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor is recommended in addition to aspirin: initial oral LD followed by MD for 12 months unless there is high bleeding risk (HBR).
A proton pump inhibitor in combination with DAPT is recommended in patients at high risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
Prasugrel recommended in P2Y12 receptor inhibitor–naïve patients proceeding to PCI (specific dosing provided); lower dosing recommended for age ≥75 years or body weight <60 kg.
Ticagrelor recommended irrespective of treatment strategy (invasive or conservative) with specified dosing.
Clopidogrel recommended when prasugrel or ticagrelor are not available, not tolerated, or contraindicated (specified LD/MD).
If patients presenting with ACS stop DAPT to undergo CABG, resume DAPT after surgery for at least 12 months.
Prasugrel may be considered in preference to ticagrelor for ACS patients who proceed to PCI (IIa).
GP IIb/IIIa receptor antagonists should be considered if there is evidence of no-reflow or a thrombotic complication during PCI (IIa).
In P2Y12 receptor inhibitor–naïve patients undergoing PCI, cangrelor may be considered (IIb).
In older ACS patients, especially if HBR, clopidogrel as the P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered (IIb).

Associated Conditions: Older ACS patients / high bleeding risk (HBR)
genes.context: The guideline repeatedly refers to the P2Y12 receptor inhibitor in ACS management: recommended in all ACS patients alongside aspirin, referenced in 'P2Y12 receptor inhibitor–naïve' patients for prasugrel and cangrelor use, and clopidogrel is mentioned as a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor option in older/HBR patients.
